citation.title: Diffusion-based cGAN framework for automated optimization and code-compliant generative design of thin-walled structures
citation.authors: Chamod Fernando, Sumudu Herath, Lowhikan Sivanantha Sarma
citation.version_coded: open-access version of record, author-uploaded copy

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: After offline training, the model generates structural layouts much faster than the conventional iterative optimization pipeline across the reported frame cases.
claim.location: abstract (qualitative); first quantitative comparison in §4.4, Table 2
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: §4.4 states average speedup over 40,000 times from Table 2; 40,000 is the stated lower bound, not an exact factor.
claim.alternatives: Abstract reports a qualitative online speed advantage; §4.4 describes a four-to-five-order-of-magnitude inference advantage; conclusion repeats lower inference times.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP-based topology optimization followed by skeletonization, SLSQP frame size/layout optimization and section assignment, following Sarma et al. [1]
baseline.hardware_ml: §2.3 and §4.2: NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPU, CUDA 12.4, PyTorch 2.4.0
baseline.problem_size: §2, §3.4: 2D frames rendered at 512×512 pixels; FE mesh size not stated
baseline.ml_time: §4.4, Table 2: 0.011–0.022 s for layout inference across 12 cases
baseline.training_time: §4.2: 100 epochs (simply supported) and 300 epochs (cantilevered); wall-clock time not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: §4.4 says offline optimization-derived dataset cost is excluded; no duration stated
baseline.quality_metric: §4.1, §4.3, Table 1: SSIM, Dice, IoU versus reference layouts; §4.6, Table 6: FE compliance, displacement, member utilization and volume of two generated examples
baseline.quality_gap: No matched ML-versus-classical compliance or volume difference for the 12 timed cases is stated; §4.6 reports FE values for two generated examples only.

R1.evidence: §4.4, Table 2: inference times are compared with complete classical optimization times for 12 inputs, but no matched objective or volume comparison accompanies these cases; §4.6 checks only two generated examples.

R2.evidence: §4.2 identifies the ML GPU; §4.4, Table 2 does not state classical hardware, solver, or a hardware-matching justification. No R2(a–e) criterion can be established.

R3.evidence: §4.4 explicitly limits the speedup to inference, but gives neither data-generation nor training duration and no break-even calculation; §4.2 gives epochs only.

R4.evidence: §4.6, Figure 15 and Table 6 FE-check two representative generated frames with volume and constraints, but gives no selection rule or failure rate for all generated designs.

reporting.n_test_cases: §4.4, Table 2: 12 timing cases (6 simply supported, 6 cantilevered); §4.6: two FE-checked generated designs

notes: Author-uploaded public full text on ResearchGate; publisher PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403. §4.4 explicitly says the speed comparison concerns online inference. The FE checks in §4.6 are for two representative outputs, without a classical quality comparison for Table 2's timed cases.
